div.head: ECf 32 C 5
div.ab: Multi uero Angli ceperunt uxores suas de sanguine et genere Anglorum Germanie, et quidam Angli ceperunt uxores suas de sanguine et genere Scotorum; proceres uero Scotorum, et Scotti fere omnes, ceperunt uxores suas de optimo sanguine et genere Anglorum Germanie; et ita fuerunt tunc temporis per uniuersum regnum Britannie duo in carne una.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 658 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 C …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
Liebermann marks “duo” with a dagger for his marginal reference to Genesis 2, 24.

note.seg: seit 1100 heirathete das Englische Königshaus in die Dynastien von Schottland, Deutschland, Wales, Bretagne, Sachsen im Dienste Grossbritannischer und Europäischer Politik: was vielleicht der Londoner Phantasie Anregung gab. Englischer Adel heirathete manchmal in Wales und Schottland. In der Hauptsache träumt der Londoner; statt Angli setzt er Norwegienses 32 E 2

from 1100 the English royal house married into the dynasties of Scotland, Germany, Wales, Brittany and Saxony in the service of British and European policy: which perhaps stimulated the Londoner’s imagination. The English nobility sometimes married into Wales and Scotland. In the main the Londoner is dreaming; instead of Angli he puts Norwegienses at 32 E 2
